fields.name: Barnard's Star
fields.blurb: The fastest-moving star in the sky: 10.4 arcsec per year, about 1.7 SPHEREx pixels.

fields.name: Epsilon Indi B
fields.blurb: A pair of brown dwarfs 12 light-years away, moving 4.7 arcsec per year.

fields.name: WISE 0855-0714
fields.blurb: The coldest known brown dwarf (about 250 K), moving 8.1 arcsec per year. The challenge coordinates are its 2010 WISE position; by 2026 it is 2 arcmin further west.

fields.name: RW Aurigae
fields.blurb: A young T Tauri binary with deep, irregular dimming events.

fields.name: R Draconis
fields.blurb: A Mira variable with a 246-day period, close to the north ecliptic pole where SPHEREx returns very often.

fields.name: Asteroid (52) Europa crossing
fields.blurb: Main-belt asteroid (52) Europa, magnitude 12.2, crosses this patch of sky in ten hours on 20-21 August 2025: it is in 24 frames and absent from the other 87. Detectors 3 and 6 only (1.6-2.4 and 4.4-5.0 micron).

fields.name: Pluto drifting
fields.blurb: Pluto, magnitude 14.5, creeps 12 pixels across this patch between 4 and 10 October 2025 (18 frames) and is gone in the other survey passes: what a slow, distant solar-system body looks like to SPHEREx. Detector 2 only (1.1-1.7 micron).
